newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL manufacturers say power hike hit exports firms.
newsitem.headline: KL manufacturers say power hike hit exports firms.

text.p: Malaysia manufacturers said on Saturday that export-oriented manufacturers would be hardest-hit by new electricity tariff hikes announced last Wednesday.
"Export-oriented manufacturesrs would be the ones worst hit by the tariff hike," the Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) said in a statement.

"The immediate increase will definitely affect the margins of those goods contracted by the foreign buyers, whose contracts were signed very much earlier on, and the production cost was based on the old rates," it said.

Those affected include electrical and electronics manufacturers which account for 53 percent of manufactured exports, and contribute to 20.6 percent of the purchase of electricity from Tenaga, the FMM said.
The government earlier this week allowed power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd to raise electricity charges by 8.3 percent, or 1.8 Malaysian cents per unit to 23.5 cents, from May 1.
FMM said the 1.8 cent per unit increase would raise tariffs from 7.5 percent for low voltage industrial users to 18 percent for high voltage/off peak industrial users.
"This is definitely higher than the average 8.0 percent increase experienced by other sectors," the statement said.
It said the tariff hike "would undoubtedly increase the cost of doing business and would pose financial burden to the manufactiring sector as well as affect their competitiveness".
By FMM's estimates, Malaysian manufacturers consume 85.6 percent of power generated by Tenaga.
